description: This team will do great things!
summary:
You’re alone on Mars, keeping a small outpost alive. Your mission is to survive ten sols—ten in-game days.

Keep an eye on oxygen, power, water, and food. They decrease over time, so visit the matching station and use its prompt to refill that resource. If your food or water runs out, your health starts to fall. Health won’t regenerate on its own.

When trouble comes up, open ARES. Each alert gives you two or three choices. Your decisions can change your resources immediately or bring consequences later.

A greenhouse problem might force you to choose between protecting the crops, spending supplies, or accepting a smaller harvest. There may not be a perfect answer—only the trade-off you’re willing to make.

Watch for sandstorms. Get inside the habitat: staying outside costs health, and the solar array can’t recharge power during the storm.

Some greenhouse events draw on NASA’s EDEN ISS study in Antarctica. In 2018, its 12.5-square-metre cultivation area produced more than 268 kilograms of edible biomass. It’s a real-world growing experiment to learn from.

Manage your supplies, respond to emergencies, and make it to Sol Ten. Can you keep the outpost running?
details:
Project Details: Mars Outpost Survival Simulator

  • What it does: A Roblox survival game where the player manages a Mars outpost for ten sols. They maintain oxygen, power, water, and food, respond to ARES alerts, and shelter during sandstorms.
  • Benefits: Builds awareness of resource management, emergency decisions, and the challenges of growing food in isolated environments.
  • Intended impact: Make space and life-support challenges engaging and understandable through interactive play.
  • Tools and technology: Roblox Studio and Luau scripting, Roblox parts and terrain, and NASA’s EDEN ISS greenhouse study in the OSDR. No special hardware or external AI service is required.
  • What makes it creative: ARES presents scripted challenges with competing choices and immediate or delayed consequences, so players experience how decisions affect the outpost.
  • Factors considered: The two-day deadline, a manageable game scope, clear controls, balanced survival resources, and responsible use of real research as an Earth-based analog for Mars.

Data note: The EDEN ISS study informs greenhouse content.
